page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 virtual CPUs (4 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor and includes 33 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.se1.2xlarge delivers modest compute performance. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks are also relatively weak, falling into the bottom 10%. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks (256 MB) performs in the average range, as do Passmark CPU and physics tests. Large-model LLM inference speeds are poor, though small-model (135M) inference achieves average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.2xlarge offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-frequency CPU performance. The primary tradeoff is the lower single-core and multi-core processing speed compared to newer compute-optimized instances. This server is best suited for memory-bound applications, caching layers, small-scale database hosting, and lightweight enterprise applications that benefit from a 64 GB memory footprint without demanding intensive parallel processing.
